title: Pin firstmate main to a SHA at study start, mount it read-only
summary: When a study job is dispatched, Athena's Rust code resolves firstmate's main on GitHub to a commit SHA, records it in the job's records, and materialises that tree read-only inside the agents' working directory. A test, using a fake source, shows the core's study dispatch calls the pinning code.

defaults_applied.how: The pinning is written in Rust, with no shell or Python helper.
The new module has unit tests and a core-level test, and clippy and cargo test must pass.
Reuse athena-git, which wraps the git binary, or a maintained crate before writing a bespoke client; record the call.
Read-only is enforced by file permissions and tool grants, not by a prompt instruction.
One focused change limited to the study start path.
Behavior is checked by running the tests.
Only the public repository URL and SHA are recorded; no credentials.
Details such as the record location and the config field were recovered from the repository and BRIEF.md lines 275 and 395.

assumptions: The pin is made by Athena's Rust code (the git binary via athena-git, or a maintained crate), not by an agent.
Resolution and fetch go through a trait so tests use a local fake repository and need no network.
The pin is recorded as a field in the job's records (repository URL, ref 'main', resolved SHA), written before the producer starts.
Read-only means the files are marked non-writable and the tree is placed in a directory the agents' tool grants cannot write to; no git history is needed in it.
Only the study capability triggers the pin; the change capability is untouched.
The URL is configured in athena.toml's study section rather than hard-coded; if the config schema needs a field, that is a governance edit named in a criterion.
The 'core calls it' test drives the core's study dispatch (athena-core run path) with a fake pinner and asserts it was called once with the firstmate URL and main, and that the recorded SHA matches.

acceptance_criteria.text: A pinning module or trait exists in Rust that takes a repository URL and ref and returns a full 40-hex commit SHA, plus a function that exports the tree at that SHA into a given directory.
The core's dispatch path calls the pinner when the accepted reading's capability is study, before the producer is invoked, and not for the change capability.
The resolved SHA, the URL and the ref are written into a committed job record, with a schema/record type update if needed.
The pinned tree is placed inside the agents' working directory with files read-only (no write permission bits), and the study producer/verifier grants do not allow writing into it.

A test in athena-core with a fake pinner passes: run `cargo test -p athena-core`; it asserts the study dispatch invokes the pinner once with https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate and main, and records the SHA it returned.
A test shows the change capability dispatch does not call the pinner: run `cargo test`.
A test of the export function with a local temporary git repository checks the tree contents match the pinned commit and every file is read-only: run `cargo test`.
`cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes, and `cargo test` passes for the whole workspace.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry, and the design doc or decisions note records the choice of git-via-athena-git versus a crate.

out_of_scope: Actually running the firstmate study or making any claim about firstmate's contents.
departures: The reference costs are raised somewhat. This touches the core dispatch path, record schemas and a new fake-based test seam, so it needs more work than the typical job. The reading also rests on several assumptions (record location, config field).
